themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 8 this week versus a baseline of 2.2 per week (256% increase, z-score 4.43), marking the most recent and acute quality-of-life deterioration in CD 314 and suggesting either coordinated vandalism or a breakdown in enforcement response.
evidence: 8 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score 4.43)
Highest z-score among recent spikes, indicating most statistically significant anomaly in current data
Spike is current-week, not lagged — indicates active, ongoing problem rather than historical backlog
reporting_angles: Survey visible graffiti hotspots in Midwood/Ocean Parkway neighborhoods; interview residents and local business owners about whether they've noticed increased vandalism
Contact NYPD and Sanitation Department to determine whether there's a known pattern, coordinated crew, or resource gap in rapid-response removal

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 3 this week from a baseline of 0.5 per week (500% increase, z-score 2.89), a sharp emerging problem that may signal either a bike-share or personal bike disposal issue in the district.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score 2.89)
Second-most-recent spike (tied with graffiti for this-week emergence)
No prior context or sustained trend — represents sudden emergence rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Document locations of abandoned bikes; determine whether they are personal bikes, Citi Bike units, or scooter company inventory
Interview local residents and business owners about whether they're aware of dumping or abandonment activity; check with Citi Bike about any known issues in the district

themes_detail.label: Air quality emergency alert
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints surged to 5 two weeks ago from a baseline of 0.6 per week (700% increase, z-score 9.04, highest severity spike), indicating a significant but time-lagged environmental or industrial event that warrants urgent investigation into sources.
evidence: 5 air quality complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 9.04, highest z-score in dataset)
Highest severity rating among all spikes; indicates sustained environmental concern
Timing suggests event occurred 2 weeks ago — may be ongoing or may have resolved; warrants current verification
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with DEP air quality monitoring stations, EPA AirNow data, and industrial facility reports (Con Edison, manufacturers, waste transfer) to identify source during that 2-week window
Interview residents who filed complaints about symptoms; check whether complaints clustered geographically (e.g., near Coney Island Ave or industrial corridor)
Determine whether source was acute (fire, spill, industrial accident) or chronic (nearby facility ramping operations); assess ongoing risk

themes_detail.label: Street noise spike in Midwood
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 100 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 32.2 per week (210% increase, z-score 3.31), indicating a significant, localized noise event or construction activity that may be ongoing or recently concluded.
evidence: 100 noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 32.2 weekly baseline (210% spike, z-score 3.31)
Spike is lagged by 2 weeks, but spike magnitude suggests significant resident impact
Street/sidewalk noise distinct from residential noise (separate category), suggesting outdoor source: construction, event, or traffic pattern change
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with DOB building permit data (347 filings in last 90 days, 267 alterations) to identify active construction sites; determine whether a major project ramped up 2 weeks ago
Contact 311 to geocode complaint locations; determine whether noise clustered near Coney Island Ave, Flatbush Ave, or other major thoroughfares
Interview residents near clusters about source and whether noise has subsided or continues

themes_detail.label: Derelict vehicle dumping trend
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints rose to 19 last week from a baseline of 9.9 per week (92% increase, z-score 2.8), indicating an emerging problem with abandoned or non-operational vehicles that may reflect broader lot-clearing or commercial activity in the district.
evidence: 19 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 9.9 weekly baseline (92% spike, z-score 2.8)
Spike is recent (last week) and sustained above baseline
Consistent with 500% spike in abandoned bikes — suggests broader trend of asset abandonment or dumping in district
reporting_angles: Document locations of derelict vehicles reported; determine whether they cluster near vacant lots, development sites (1455 Coney Island Ave, 2586 Nostrand Ave rezoning projects), or commercial areas
Contact NYPD and Sanitation to determine removal timeline and whether there's a known dumping operation or chop-shop activity
Interview neighbors about safety concerns and whether they've observed suspicious vehicle activity
